citation.title: Pedestal and Er profile evolution during an edge localized mode cycle at ASDEX Upgrade
citation.authors: M. Cavedon, T. Pütterich, E. Viezzer, F. M. Laggner, A. Burckhart, M. Dunne, R. Fischer, A. Lebschy, F. Mink, U. Stroth, M. Willensdorfer, E. Wolfrum, ASDEX Upgrade Team
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1361-6587/aa7ad0 (from the supplied record hint; not printed in the extracted text, so unverified)

topic: ELM-synchronized edge He2+ CXRS impurity Ti, density, flows and Er, compared with electron profiles from Li-BES, ECE, IDA and Thomson scattering, at ASDEX Upgrade
own_question: How do ion and electron pedestal profiles, gradients and Er recover through a type-I ELM cycle, and does Er match the neoclassical estimate?
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline conditional averaging over roughly 80 ELMs from dedicated AUG discharges. ELM onset was referenced to the divertor shunt current. Edge CXRS on the He2+ line had 65 µs acquisition; IDA electron profiles had about 100 µs. Profiles were mapped with a separatrix-shift correction and fitted with splines. The authors report that max ∇Ti recovers in about 4 ms, similar to ∇ne, while ∇Te takes about 7–8 ms. Er collapses toward L-mode-like values at the crash and recovers within about 3–4 ms. Er agrees with the neoclassical estimate within uncertainties, except a possible deviation 2–4 ms after the crash that the authors flag as uncertain.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Impurity-CXRS ion temperature at the pedestal can evolve on ELM-cycle timescales different from electron temperature, so electron-diagnostic proxies need not track the ion channel one-to-one.
claim_checks.qualification: Single AUG He2+ dataset with ELM-averaged offline analysis; this is He2+ impurity Ti, not main-ion Ti; not KSTAR and not carbon.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Edge CXRS mapping and profile behaviour are most uncertain shortly after ELM crashes (about 2 ms in this case).
claim_checks.qualification: Specific to the AUG mapping procedure and these ELMs.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Time-synchronized offline profiles only. No causal or real-time inference, and no report-arrival timing.
validation_if_relevant: Cross-checks against binned data, Thomson scattering, and NEOART at selected time points. Not applicable to nowcasting validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim BES/ECEI predicts Ti.
Do not transfer the AUG timescales to KSTAR or carbon CES.
Do not treat the Er deviation as established.
Do not equate impurity Ti with main-ion Ti.
Do not present this source as a real-time or causal method.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Useful as physics background on ion/electron decoupling and ELM-phase transients, which motivate why nowcasting with electron-side inputs is non-trivial. It is not a methods precedent.
